pair_contract.controlled_material_fact: Where the upstream-approved proof sits in the scene's tonal range: the decision-relevant subject is either a self-luminous instrument-cluster readout (upper/highlight band, destroyed by bloom and by display flicker) or a matte repaired sill and torn seat seam in the deepest cabin shade (lower/shadow band, destroyed by being crushed and by noise smear).
pair_contract.case_1_value: Proof = odometer figure and absence of lit warning lamps on the backlit instrument cluster (emissive, highlight-critical).
pair_contract.case_2_value: Proof = extent of the disclosed repaired/repainted driver's door sill and the torn seam on the driver's seat base (matte, shadow-critical, in the shaded side of the car).
held_constant_facts: Same vehicle, same Sharjah open-air row, same 2:40 pm mid-September high western sun, same nose-in-to-the-south parking heading, same shaded driver's side, same windscreen sky glare.

Same phone and same partial device evidence: a photo of the Galaxy A56 camera settings screen showing FHD1080/30 selected, UHD 4K/30 selectable, HDR10+ off, and a Pro Video mode tile — and nothing about manual ranges, alternative frame rates, lens availability in Pro Video, or HDR10+ playback behaviour.

Same operator: the lot's salesperson, non-professional, working alone, coached only by text/voice note, with no lights, reflectors, tripod, assistant or external mic; the designer cannot see the scene and only sees clips the operator sends back.

Same observed test clip from the driver's doorway: windscreen and exterior pure white with no texture, dashboard top mid grey, lower cabin near-black, and a visible auto-exposure step about two seconds in — i.e. scene contrast provably exceeds what the phone holds in one frame, and AE is drifting.

Same levers available in both cases: car is drivable with keys on hand, an empty lot stretch 20 m away allows any heading, the workshop shade bay is free for a few minutes, seats/doors/sun visors are adjustable, engine may be run.
Same 12-minute throughput window before the next unit, same afternoon heat and prior phone thermal warning, same silent-video requirement (no audio proof needed).

Same delivery requirement in both: the proof must appear in one unbroken shot that also shows enough of this car's interior to tie the proof to this vehicle, for a listing viewed full-screen on buyers' phones.
pair_contract.why: Because the test clip establishes the scene already overflows the device's single-frame range, the operator cannot hold both ends and must deliberately sacrifice one. Moving the proof from the emissive top of the range to the matte bottom inverts every consequential choice. In case 1 the proof already emits its own light: it survives only if the frame excludes the blazing windscreen and the exposure is anchored low enough that the backlit numerals do not bloom, and the dominant technical risk is refresh-rate banding across a display plus a sky specular on the cluster lens — remedies are subtractive (tighter frame, visors, door as a flag, angle change), and adding light would destroy the proof. In case 2 the proof emits nothing and sits on the car's shaded side: at no exposure value does it become judgeable while the light on it is unchanged, so the correct move is to change the light physically — reposition the car so the sun reaches the driver's side, open both driver-side doors, use the adjacent white car and hot asphalt as bounce, slide the seat rearward out of the dash shadow — then anchor exposure to the repaired panel and deliberately clip the exterior, with the dominant technical risks being noise smear on the repaired surface and, critically, light direction that flattens the repair out of visibility. A candidate that answers both with the same stance (lock exposure on the subject, keep the bright stuff out of frame) is wrong: that stance is sufficient in case 1 and materially insufficient in case 2, and the brightening case 2 requires is precisely what ruins case 1's proof.

cases.brief: You are directing the capture of one proof shot for a used-car listing. Upstream (the listing owner) has approved exactly one proof requirement for this unit's video pass: a buyer must be able to read the odometer figure on the instrument cluster and see that no warning lamps are lit, in the same unbroken shot that shows enough of this car's interior to tie that reading to this vehicle. Produce the capture plan and the actual instruction you would send the operator, plus how you will decide whether what comes back is usable before the car goes back in the row.
cases.context: Sharjah open-air used-car lot, Tuesday 2:40 pm, mid-September, clear sky, sun high and to the west. The unit is a 2017 white Toyota Corolla, second car in a row that runs east–west with all cars nose-in to the south; so the windscreen faces south into open sky and the driver's side of this car is the shaded side. The car directly beside it is white. The operator is the lot's salesperson, not a camera professional; they are on the lot alone and you are coaching them remotely by text and voice note. You cannot see the scene yourself; the only thing you will ever see is a clip they send back. They have already sent one 6-second test clip shot from the driver's doorway: in it the windscreen and everything beyond it are pure white with no texture at all, the top of the dashboard reads as mid grey, the lower half of the cabin reads as near-black, and about two seconds in, when they lean further into the door opening, the whole image visibly steps brighter on its own. The only device evidence you have is a photo they sent of the phone's camera settings screen: a Samsung Galaxy A56 running One UI, video size set to 'FHD 1080p / 30' with 'UHD 4K / 30' also listed as selectable, an 'HDR10+ recording' toggle in the off position, and the mode carousel showing Photo, Video, Portrait, Pro and Pro Video. That photo establishes only what is on that screen. It does not establish which manual parameters Pro Video exposes, any ISO or shutter range, whether any frame rate other than 30 is offered, which lenses Pro Video can use, or how an HDR10+ file will look on a buyer's phone. The finished clip will be watched full-screen on buyers' phones inside the listing.
cases.constraints: Twelve minutes for this unit before the next one is due. Operator works alone; no lights, reflectors, diffusion, tripod, gimbal, external mic or assistant — phone in hand only. Keys are on hand, the car is drivable, and there is an empty stretch of lot about 20 m away where it can be parked at any heading; moving and returning a car costs roughly two minutes each way. The workshop's roller-shutter bay is free and shaded if you want it for a few minutes. Seats, doors and sun visors may be adjusted and the engine may be run. Ambient is about 41 °C and the phone has already thrown one overheating warning earlier today. This proof shot is silent — no audio is required from it. You may only instruct; you cannot operate the camera, and nothing is complete until a clip comes back.
cases.competent_generic_baseline: Run the engine so the cluster lights up. Have the operator sit in the driver's seat, hold the phone about 40 cm from the cluster with the windscreen kept out of the top of the frame, tap the cluster to set focus and exposure and hold to lock it so it stops jumping, then record about eight steady seconds. Shoot a second, wider clip of the cabin so the listing also shows the interior. Play both back before the car goes back in the row and confirm the odometer numbers can be read when pinch-zoomed.
professional_criteria: Names the two-sided failure explicitly and resolves it by exclusion rather than compromise: with the white windscreen in frame the meter averages it and crushes the cluster, but opening up far enough to render the dark cabin blooms the backlit numerals into an unreadable glow — so the plan removes the windscreen and exterior from the frame entirely (camera at cluster height from the doorway, visors dropped, door or body used to block the sky) instead of trying to hold both ends of the range.

Kills the auto-exposure step the test clip already demonstrated: exposure and focus are set and locked on the lit readout before recording starts, and the operator is told explicitly not to change their distance, lean or angle after locking and not to re-tap mid-shot.

Treats the cluster as a self-lit display rather than a reflective object: requires a short throwaway recording inspected specifically for rolling bands or pulsing across the readout, names a concrete thing to try if banding appears (a different frame rate if one is actually offered, a shutter value if Pro Video is confirmed to expose one, or a small change of angle and distance), and states a fallback if the phone offers no alternative — without asserting any setting value the supplied screenshot does not support.

Handles the sky specular landing on the cluster's clear plastic lens as a geometry problem — change camera height, shift a few degrees off-axis, use the open door or a dropped visor to cut the reflected skylight — rather than trying to expose through it.

Delivers the one-unbroken-shot requirement as a performable path: a defined start frame that already identifies this car's interior, a stated move or reframe with a speed the operator can actually execute, and a named hold duration parked on the readout, with start point, height, distance and end point all given in physical terms rather than as style words.

Sets the legibility standard against the buyer's real viewing condition — every odometer digit and the unlit state of the warning lamps distinguishable at ordinary full-screen playback, not only under pinch-zoom — and states what result triggers an immediate reshoot while the car is still out of the row.

Treats Pro Video, HDR10+ and 4K as unverified: either asks the operator to open the mode and read back the controls actually visible on screen, or designs a plan that works on the settings the screenshot does establish, and accounts for the heat/thermal history in how long and at what setting they record.

p0_guardrail.trigger: States as established fact a capability the supplied settings photo does not show — a specific ISO or shutter range, a 24/48/60 fps option, a log or flat profile, RAW capture, manual white-balance values, or ultra-wide/telephoto availability inside Pro Video — and builds the exposure or anti-flicker instruction on it with no read-back verification step and no fallback that works without it.

cases.competent_generic_baseline: Open the driver's door and have the operator kneel outside level with the sill. Tap and hold on the repaired area to lock focus and exposure on it so it comes up bright enough to see, keeping the sky out of the top of the frame. Record about ten steady seconds along the sill, then move in closer on the torn seat seam. Play it back before the car goes back in the row and confirm the damage is visible in the clip.
professional_criteria: Recognises that the required proof is on the car's shaded side and that exposure alone cannot deliver it: the plan changes the light physically landing on the sill and seat base — repositioning the car on the empty stretch so the driver's side turns toward the western sun, opening both front and rear driver-side doors, using the adjacent white car and the bright asphalt as bounce, sliding the driver's seat fully rearward to bring the torn seam out of the dash shadow into the doorway light — and makes one explicit choice among these against the twelve-minute clock rather than listing options.

Anchors exposure deliberately to the repaired panel and the torn seam and states plainly that the exterior, windscreen and sky are allowed to clip because no required information lives there, having first placed the camera outside at sill height so the blown exterior is not sitting behind the subject in frame.

Locks exposure and focus on the damage before recording starts to kill the mid-shot auto-exposure step the test clip already demonstrated, and instructs the operator to hold their distance and angle after locking rather than re-tapping while rolling.

Sets a truth standard about extent, not existence: the buyer must be able to judge how far the repaint runs, where its edges are, and how large the tear is — so the plan specifies a light direction that rakes across the panel to reveal surface texture and the colour break, warns against the angle or flat shade in which the repair simply disappears, and rejects showing the area only in silhouette or only from a distance.

Accounts for how the phone behaves in deep shade: the played-back clip is checked full-screen for noise smearing or mushy, detail-free texture across the repaired panel, and if detail is smeared the response is to get more light onto it or move the car rather than to accept it or to crop in with digital zoom.

Delivers the one-unbroken-shot requirement as a performable path — start position, camera height, distance, the speed of any move, where to pause and for how long on the sill and on the seam, and where the shot ends — including the instruction that the operator's own shadow and the open door's shadow must not fall across the area being shown.

Defines an on-location PASS/RESHOOT test while the car is still out of the row, and names a concrete fallback if the light cannot be made to work inside the window — the free shade bay, or returning at a different hour — instead of sending back an ambiguous clip, and flags to downstream what the delivered clip is and is not authoritative for.

p0_guardrail.trigger: The plan results in the disclosed repaired sill or torn seam being unreadable in the delivered shot — framed out, left in silhouette or crushed shadow, shown only at a distance that hides its extent — or selects an angle, light direction or exposure specifically because it makes the repair less conspicuous, or defers making the damage visible to post-production, the still photos or the listing text.
